operator_io_quirks: No primary keys on either table; playstore.App is 9659-distinct over 10840 rows (near-unique but not unique), user_reviews.App is 1074-distinct over 64286 rows (many-to-one).
FK user_reviews.App -> playstore.App points to a NON-UNIQUE parent column; upstream fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws with replacement from parent values, so duplicates are expected and fine.
Column name 'Content Rating' has a space; must be double-quoted everywhere (DDL, INSERT, sampler keys).

All columns declared TEXT except Rating REAL and Reviews INTEGER; Size/Installs/Price/Sentiment_Polarity/Sentiment_Subjectivity are TEXT storing numbers/units ('19M', '10,000+', '$4.99', '0.5333...').
user_reviews.Translated_Review and Sentiment* have storage class 'null' present despite null_rate 0.0 (literal string 'nan' rows); declared TEXT so String fuzzer, not Number.
playstore.Rating has 13.6% NULLs (storage 'null'); declared REAL -> Number fuzzer, elements include None which Base drops.
playstore.Type has literal string 'NaN' as a value (distinct=3: Free/Paid/NaN) — not a NULL, a real string.
App names contain unicode (Chinese, en-dash '–'), '&', spaces; String fuzzer CHARSET is ASCII-only so fresh draws won't reproduce them.
user_reviews has 64286 rows > playstore 10840; FK child is the LARGER table, so parent values are heavily reused.
No indexes, views, or triggers in DDL; empty clone is just the two CREATE TABLEs.
playstore.App samples truncated at 40 chars in facts but full values are longer; String length range derives from element lengths.
Installs values like '10,000+' contain commas and '+'; Price mixes '0' and '$4.99' — String fuzzer will contaminate these.
operator_ts_expectations: playstore.App / user_reviews.App: String fuzzer, length range from element lengths, fresh draws over a-zA-Z 0-9() — will NOT produce realistic app names (no unicode, no '&'), driving FN on name-equality/join predicates.

Category/Type/Content Rating/Genres/Sentiment: String fuzzer with small element pools (3-119 distinct); fresh random strings dominate at p=0.2, so equality predicates on these enums often match nothing -> FN.
Size/Installs/Price: String fuzzer treats '19M','10,000+','$4.99' as opaque strings; contaminate() adds/drops chars, producing implausible values -> FN on LIKE/format predicates, FP on loose matches.
Rating (REAL): Number fuzzer scale=4, range [-10^4,10^4] plus +-0.01/0.02 perturbation; original values are 1.0-5.0 so fresh draws are wildly out of range -> FN on Rating>4.5 style predicates.
Reviews (INTEGER): Number fuzzer range [-10^4,10^4] with +-1/+-2 perturbation; original up to 215644, so large-count predicates (Reviews>100000) rarely satisfied -> FN.

Sentiment_Polarity/Subjectivity (TEXT): String fuzzer, not Number — numeric-looking strings get str(i+1)/str(i-1) neighbors but fresh draws are random ASCII, so range predicates on these TEXT columns behave oddly.

FK user_reviews.App draws from playstore.App final values with replacement; since playstore.App is near-unique, join cardinality is roughly preserved but duplicates appear -> possible FP on COUNT(DISTINCT) queries.
No PKs: sample_fresh_primary_keys is a no-op; drop_unique_duplicates only fires on single-column unique indexes (none here), so duplicate rows are NOT removed -> FP on DISTINCT/COUNT queries.

Type='NaN' string and Rating NULLs: predicates like Type='Free' AND Rating IS NULL interact; TS may generate NULLs for Rating (Number fuzzer can emit None? no — Base drops None, so Rating never NULL in generated) -> FN on IS NULL queries.
String contaminate() at 0.5 rate on every sample means even element-derived values get mutated half the time -> many near-miss values, FP on LIKE '%...%' and equality.
Small enum columns (Type 3, Sentiment 4, Content Rating 6) with p=0.2 fresh draws: ~20% of rows get random strings, so GROUP BY on these yields spurious groups -> FP on group-count queries.
